content: SAMPLE. I am Yaman, a software engineer at a WordPress agency. I build websites and plugins in PHP and JavaScript, I contribute to open source, and I spend a lot of my spare time automating things with n8n and AI tools.

SAMPLE. I got into programming by tinkering, breaking things and fixing them again. That curiosity turned into a career building for the web, mostly with WordPress and PHP. Over time I moved from just shipping features to caring about how teams work, how code stays maintainable, and lately how AI agents can take repetitive work off people's plates.

SAMPLE. My number one superpower is getting unstuck fast. When something is broken or unclear, I reproduce it, narrow it down and find the real cause instead of patching symptoms. People tend to bring me the weird bugs because I enjoy them.

SAMPLE. The three areas I want to grow in are: first, delegating earlier instead of trying to do everything myself; second, communicating progress more often, not only when something is finished; and third, going deeper on system design and evaluation for AI agents so I can judge their quality with data, not gut feeling.

SAMPLE. A common misconception coworkers have about me is that I am quiet because I am not interested. Really I am thinking it through before I speak, and once I have a clear picture I am very vocal and opinionated.

SAMPLE. I push my boundaries by picking work slightly beyond what I know, like contributing to an open source PHP AI client library where the maintainers have high standards. I set a small, concrete goal, ship something, get feedback, and repeat. Being a bit uncomfortable is usually a sign I am learning.

SAMPLE. My core skills are PHP and WordPress development, JavaScript, building integrations against third party APIs, workflow automation in n8n, and using AI coding tools every day to move faster while still reviewing everything carefully.

SAMPLE. I like to understand the goal before writing code, keep changes small and reviewable, and test things the way a real user would hit them. I prefer simple, boring solutions that are easy to maintain over clever ones.

SAMPLE. A project I am proud of is an internal automation that turned a tedious manual reporting task into a workflow that runs on its own. It saved the team hours every week and, more importantly, people stopped dreading that task.

SAMPLE. Once I shipped a fix quickly without reproducing the bug end to end, and it did not actually solve the problem the user saw. The lesson I took is to always reproduce the issue the way the user hits it before changing anything.

SAMPLE. I am excited about AI agents because they let small teams do much more. I already use AI coding tools daily, and I see the next step as agents that handle whole workflows reliably, with good guardrails and evaluation so people can trust them.

SAMPLE. In a team I try to be the person who unblocks others. I review code carefully but kindly, write down decisions so nobody has to guess, and I am happy to pair on a hard problem rather than leave someone stuck.
